body: Tops (each appeared before or at the 1992, 1994, 2000, 2008, 2018, 2021 and 2024 peaks): (1) issuance boom with falling issuer quality - 1993-96 small IPOs, Reliance Power (Jan 2008), 2021 loss-making tech IPOs, 2024 SME IPOs subscribed hundreds of times; (2) leverage or unusual funding - bank receipts (1992), badla and co-op bank money (2000), project/land loans (2007), NBFC lending (2017-18), retail F&O (2021-24); (3) narrative stocks valued on non-cash metrics - land banks, order books, GMV, 'nation-building'; (4) valuation extremes - Sensex P/E 27-35x, Nifty >24x, market cap/GDP >120-150%, smallcap/midcap P/E above large caps; (5) breadth divergence - small caps peak first (Jan 2018, Sept/Dec 2024) while the index makes new highs; (6) regulator warnings/tightening (SEBI on SME IPOs 2024, MF stress tests 2024). Bottoms (2001-03, Oct 2008-Mar 2009, Aug 2013, Mar 2020, early 2025/2026 for small caps): P/E ~11-15x, mcap/GDP <70%, IPO drought, FPI capitulation (record outflows, ownership at multi-year lows - 15.8% in 2026), rupee panic followed by a forceful RBI/government response, and defensives leading. No signal times the turn; combinations of 3+ have marked zones where adding risk (bottoms) or trimming it (tops) paid off over 2-5 years.

data.bottom_signals: P/E 11-15x, mcap/GDP<70%, IPO drought, FPI capitulation, currency panic + policy response
data.top_signals: issuance quality, leverage, narrative valuation, P/E/mcap-GDP extremes, breadth divergence, regulator action

title: Recurring signals that marked Indian market tops and bottoms (1992-2026)

body: Part A: 131 case_study records -> 106 point-in-time episodes (43 traps: 19 fraud, 15 leverage, 9 busts; 63 winners incl. 9 false alarms); flags counted only if public before T (else unknown). Current hard set: traps 8 Y / 31 N / 4 U, winners 0 / 62 / 1; all 8 catches were fraud cases via judgment signals (H1a Satyam, H1b Vakrangee/Manpasand/Cox&Kings, H1c Wirecard/Rajesh Exports, H5 Gitanjali, H4 SME basket). Leverage blow-ups 0/15, busts 0/9. Graded flags fired on 22/28 known traps AND 21/24 known winners; '3+ graded flags' hit 8 traps and 7 winners (HAL, BSE, Mazagon, Trent, Netflix-2019, SMCI, Eternal). In-sample caveat: the hard rules were written from these traps. Part B: 580-co PEAD sample, snapshot 30-Sep-2020, 495 priced: base rates 5y loss>50% 1.8%, >3x 54.5%; ANY(R1-R4) flagged 139: loss50 2.9% vs 1.4% (p 0.28), x3 64% vs 51% (p 0.009). Survivor-only, bull-market, success-conditioned sample -> cannot see delisted traps. Verdict: keep judgment fraud signals hard; make auditor exit a hard EXIT trigger; keep pledge graded; demote cash-flow tests to questions; move P/E to stage 5; add solvency flags (untested).

data.unlocks: calibrated stage-2 gate; nightly detector set; re-test on point-in-time universe with dead companies

title: Hard-filter back-test (21-Nov-2026): judgment fraud signals caught 8/39 known traps with 0/62 winners rejected; no mechanical rule (CFO/PAT, pledge, auditor exit, debt+neg CFO) earned hard status; solvency is an uncovered gap
